senses.gloss: स्थेम in comp. for स्थेमन्.
स्थेम—भाज् mfn. firm, strong, Śiś.
स्थेम॑न् m. (fr. स्थिर) firmness, stability, TS.; Br.; Kāṭh.
continuance, duration (˚म्ना ind. ‘perseveringly’), HYog.
the state of standing or stopping still, rest, Naiṣ.
स्थेमन् , स्थैर्य &c. See p. 1265.
स्थेम्ना (˚म्ना), ind., ‘perseveringly’
स्थेय mf(आ)n. to be stationed or fixed or settled &c.
placed (as water in a jar), ŚāṅkhGṛ.
स्थेय n. (it is) to be stood still, R.
(it is) to be stood firm (in battle), BhP.
(it is) to be stayed or remained in (loc.), R.; Hariv. &c.
(attention) is to be fixed on (loc.), MBh.; R. &c.
(it is) to be behaved or acted or proceeded (with instr. ind.p. or adv.), Hariv.; Bhartṛ.; Rājat.
स्थेय m. a person chosen to settle a dispute between two parties, an arbitrator, umpire, judge, Rājat.; Hit.
a domestic priest, L.
स्थे॑यस् mfn. (compar. of स्थिर) firmer, stronger, more important or worthy of consideration, very firm or strong, TS. &c.
very continuous or constant, Rājat.
very resolute, Sāh.
स्थेयी-कृत mfn. (स्थेयी for स्थेय, m.) made an arbitrator or umpire or judge, Kathās.
स्थेष्ठ mfn. (superl. of स्थिर) most fixed, very firm or strong or durable, Pāṇ. vi, 4, 157.
